Subject: Developing a cost-effective shipping plan for our network (whole-unit loads only)
Date: [Insert date]

Situation
We operate a network of sources (warehouses, factories, and distribution centers) that supply products to multiple destinations (stores, customers, and regional hubs). Freight spend is a significant cost driver, and lane rates vary meaningfully across the network. At the same time, service commitments require that every destination receives what it needs on time. Shipments must be in whole unit quantities; no partial loads are permitted.

Problem
We need a single, executable shipping plan that:
- Assigns whole-unit shipments from each source to each destination.
- Does not exceed available inventory or shipping capacity at any source.
- Fulfills the required quantities at every destination.
- Selects routes in a way that achieves the lowest total transportation cost without compromising service levels.

Why this matters
- Reduces total freight spend by steering volume to lower-cost routes where feasible.
- Protects on-time, in-full performance and customer satisfaction by aligning supply with each location’s needs.
- Prevents stock imbalances by respecting source limits and avoiding over-allocations.
- Creates a transparent, defensible plan for carrier tendering and daily execution.

Approach and next steps
- Validate the latest supply availability, destination requirements, and per-route shipping costs (see Annex).
- Build a baseline plan that meets all destination needs using whole-unit shipments only.
- Review hotspots where demand and supply are tight or where only high-cost lanes are available, and evaluate practical mitigations (load consolidation, alternate lanes, or inventory repositioning).
- Confirm the plan with operations and transportation teams and lock it for tendering, with an exceptions process for any late changes.
